the enzymes of the bacterial antibiotic resistance arsenal have evolved to inactivate the majority of antibiotics in clinical use, that these enzymes are highly specific for their substrates, and that these enzymes are the targets for the development of the next generation of antibiotics.
the chemical biology of antibiotic inactivation enzymes provides a rich source of information that can be leveraged for the discovery of next generation antimicrobial therapies.

the discovery and characterization of enzymes that inactivate antibiotics, and how this knowledge can inform the development of new antibiotics.
the mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in bacteria.
the chemical biology of the enzymes that inactivate antibiotics and how they can be targeted for therapeutic intervention.

we have made significant progress in our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of resistance.

we have discovered the mechanisms by which antibiotic resistance enzymes function and how these can be targeted by small molecules to inhibit the enzymes.

the chemical diversity of the antibiotic resistome is vast and is likely to continue to increase as the number of antibiotics and the number of antibiotic targets increase.
